question.en: How is the colour of the vestments decided?

answer.en: The colour is governed by the Office or Mass actually being celebrated, not simply by today's calendar heading.

detail.en: The 1960 Code names five usual Roman liturgical colours: white, red, green, violet and black. The relevant feast, permitted votive or Requiem Mass, and sometimes the exact stage of a rite determine which applies.

question.en: What do the five usual Roman liturgical colours correspond to?

answer.en: White is associated with Christmas, Eastertide and many non-martyr feasts; red with Pentecost and martyrs; green with specified weeks after Epiphany and Pentecost; violet with penitential seasons and certain rites; black with Masses of the Dead and part of Good Friday.

detail.en: These are rubrical associations, not exhaustive statements of colour symbolism. Feast and rite exceptions matter: a seasonal green feria can have an authorized votive Mass in another colour.

question.en: Why might rose vestments appear on only two Sundays?

answer.en: Rose may replace violet for the Office and Mass of Gaudete Sunday, the Third Sunday of Advent, and Laetare Sunday, the Fourth Sunday of Lent.

detail.en: This is a permitted option, not an additional ordinary liturgical season, nor a permission applying to every weekday of the surrounding week.

question.en: What do first, second, third and fourth class mean?

answer.en: The four classes indicate the rank of liturgical days. Together with the table of precedence, they help decide which observance takes priority when several coincide.

detail.en: The 1962 system distinguishes Sundays, ferias, vigils, feasts and octaves as well as their classes. The class is not the form in which Mass is offered: first-class does not mean Solemn Mass.

answers.title: Why a saint's feast is not celebrated

question.en: Why is a saint's feast printed for today but not celebrated at Mass?

answer.en: A higher-ranking Sunday, feria, vigil or feast may take precedence. Depending on the precise rubrics, the lower observance may be commemorated, transferred or omitted.

detail.en: For instance, Lenten third-class ferias rank above third-class feasts. Only certain impeded first-class feasts enjoy accidental transfer; not every displaced saint's feast automatically moves to Sunday.

question.en: Why might a church celebrate a feast not found on the general calendar?

answer.en: The 1962 rite recognizes both the universal calendar and proper calendars of places, churches, dioceses and religious communities.

detail.en: An actual church can have its own titular, dedication or patronal observance. The priest normally follows the calendar applicable to the church or oratory where Mass is celebrated; a generic internet calendar cannot determine every local case.

answers.title: Why the Mass differs from today's Office

question.en: Why is today's Mass different from the Office or calendar day?

answer.en: The Mass normally follows the day's Office, but the 1962 Missal also permits properly qualified votive Masses and Masses of the Dead.

detail.en: Certain feast Masses and external solemnities have further special rules. One must know which Mass was actually selected, and whether it was permitted; neither the season nor the civil date alone suffices.

answers.title: Low, Sung and Solemn are not feast ranks

question.en: Does a first-class feast mean a Solemn Mass?

answer.en: No. The class belongs to the liturgical day. Low, Missa Cantata and Solemn describe the mode and ministers of the Mass.

detail.en: Under rubric 271, a sung Mass without the sacred ministers is Missa Cantata; when celebrated with deacon and subdeacon it is Solemn Mass. Pontifical Mass has additional episcopal ceremonies.

question.en: Why are red vestments used for palms, but violet for the Mass?

answer.en: The 1962 rubrics prescribe red for the blessing and procession of palms. The Mass of Palm Sunday belongs to Passiontide and uses violet.

detail.en: These are successive ritual stages of one day, not contradictory calendar entries. An actual procession should be shown only when that event is part of the represented celebration.

question.en: Why do the vestments change colour during Good Friday?

answer.en: The 1962 Good Friday liturgical action prescribes black up to—but not including—the Communion portion, when violet is used.

detail.en: The day is not celebrated with the ordinary Mass. The distinct actions of the Good Friday liturgy must be taken from the printed 1962 ceremonial, without silently importing pre-1955 practice or the 2008 wording of the solemn prayers.

question.en: Why are crucifixes and sacred images covered in Passiontide?

answer.en: The 1962 tradition prescribes violet veiling of specified crosses and images as Passiontide begins, before Palm Sunday.

detail.en: The practice is traditionally associated with the growing solemnity of the Passion and Christ's hiddenness in John 8:59. Exact obligations differ for altar images, other images and Stations of the Cross; do not assume that every sacred image is covered.

sources.locator: Passiontide veiling and the tradition's development

answers.title: When crosses and images are unveiled

question.en: When are the veils removed?

answer.en: Crosses are unveiled for their Good Friday veneration; the other images remain covered until the Gloria of the Easter Vigil.

detail.en: This rule must be applied to the relevant physical object and liturgical stage, not treated as one global image-toggle at the stroke of midnight.

sources.locator: Reproduction and translation of printed-1962 Saturday-before-Passion rubric

question.en: Why does the 1962 calendar retain only three octaves?

answer.en: The common 1962 calendar celebrates the octaves of Christmas, Easter and Pentecost; older octaves are not automatically retained.

detail.en: Easter and Pentecost have first-class octaves. Christmas has a second-class octave, although its octave day is first class. Earlier editions must not be substituted without an explicit historical-mode label.

question.en: Why are prayers for another observance added to the Mass?

answer.en: A commemoration preserves a secondary liturgical observance through prescribed prayers without replacing the principal Mass.

detail.en: The 1960 Code distinguishes privileged and ordinary commemorations and sets different limits for first-, second-, third- and fourth-class days and for certain sung Masses. These are not optional additions at will.

question.en: Why are red vestments used at Pentecost and during its octave?

answer.en: Under the 1962 rubrics, red belongs to the Mass of the Vigil of Pentecost and continues through the liturgical octave until None on the following Saturday.

detail.en: Pentecost retains a first-class octave in the 1962 calendar. This must not be conflated with older versions of the Pentecost Vigil ceremonies.

answers.title: The Rosary Mass on a Sunday

question.en: Why might a Sunday Mass honour Our Lady of the Rosary although the feast is dated 7 October?

answer.en: The 1962 Missal expressly allows an external solemnity of Our Lady of the Rosary on the first Sunday of October under its prescribed conditions.

detail.en: An external solemnity is a permitted celebration of the feast's Mass for the faithful without transferring its Office to that day. It is not an unrestricted license to replace any Sunday Mass.

answers.title: Not every Rogation date has a procession

question.en: Does the Rogation date mean this church holds a procession?

answer.en: No. The 1960 rubrics expressly accommodate local decisions and circumstances: a procession may take place, or special supplications may be prescribed instead.

detail.en: The Greater Litanies ordinarily fall on 25 April and the Lesser Litanies before Ascension, but the local Ordinary and the actual celebration must be known before showing a procession or its Mass as occurring.

question.en: Why is Holy Thursday's Mass celebrated in white despite Lent?

answer.en: The Mass of the Lord's Supper is assigned white vestments by the 1960 rubrics, as a specific exception to the violet Lenten season.

detail.en: The subsequent transfer of the Blessed Sacrament and the stripping of the altars are separate ceremonies with their own sequencing. The Mandatum must not be assumed unless actually celebrated.

question.en: Why are white vestments and blessed candles used on Candlemas?

answer.en: The 1960 Code specifies white for the blessing and procession of candles on the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary, 2 February.

detail.en: The blessing of candles, any distribution and any procession must be represented as the applicable ceremony, not inferred to have occurred at every church from the date alone.

answers.title: Lenten weekday outranks a third-class saint

question.en: Why does a Lenten weekday sometimes take precedence over a saint's feast?

answer.en: Under the 1960 precedence rules, third-class ferias of Lent and Passiontide ordinarily outrank third-class feasts.

detail.en: This is different from many third-class Advent ferias before 17 December, which yield to a third-class feast. Any required seasonal commemoration is resolved separately under the rubric limits.
